headline_marked: ICT-2: [[Obaidul Quader and 6 others sentenced to death]] for July uprising crimes
headline: ICT-2: Obaidul Quader and 6 others sentenced to death for July uprising crimes
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 convicted senior Awami League leaders for crimes against humanity, including murder and persecution during the mass uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six other senior party and affiliated leaders to death for crimes against humanity during the July-August mass uprising.

The other convicts include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary Bahauddin Nasim, Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, General Secretary Moinul Hossain Khan Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain, and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Enan.
The tribunal found the convicts guilty of multiple charges, including murder and persecution during the crackdown on protesters. All the accused have been absconding throughout the legal proceedings.
The court also ordered the confiscation of 50 percent of the movable and immovable properties of Quader, Arafat, Nasim, Parash, and Nikhil to compensate victims and the families of those killed.

Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, chairman of the tribunal, delivered a summary of the 557-page verdict, which weighed approximately 25kg. The trial lasted seven months with 29 prosecution witnesses testifying.

Shortly after the verdict, a crude bomb exploded near the Supreme Court gate. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that CCTV footage identified suspects who could be 'AL miscreants', and an investigation is underway.
More than 100 pro-AL lawyers staged a silent protest on the Supreme Court premises, chanting 'Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu' in response to the judgment.

headline_marked: DB [[arrests two over death of headteacher]] in front of parliament
headline: DB arrests two over death of headteacher in front of parliament
summary: The Detective Branch has arrested two alleged muggers and recovered a motorcycle and mobile phone linked to the fatal attack on a primary school headteacher.
details: The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police has arrested two alleged muggers, Khokon and Rajib, in connection with the death of a primary school headteacher.
The arrests follow an investigation into an incident where Ranjila Parvin, 56, was killed after being pulled from a rickshaw by muggers in front of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban.
DB officers recovered a motorcycle allegedly used in the crime from Bhashantek, along with the victim's mobile phone.
The incident occurred on August 29 when Parvin, a headteacher from Bogura, was in Dhaka for eye treatment and was attacked at dawn.
She sustained critical injuries after falling from the rickshaw during the mugging attempt and later passed away.
This development comes 16 days after the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) had previously arrested two other individuals and recovered a different motorcycle.
Questions were raised regarding the discrepancy in the color of the motorcycle shown by RAB compared to the incident footage.
Additional Commissioner (DB) Shafiqul Islam is scheduled to brief reporters on the latest arrests and findings.
